name: Burako Argentinean
description: Burako is a Canasta-like Rummy game played in Argentina using 106 numbered tiles (similar to Rummikub tiles). Four players in partnerships meld sequences (escaleras) and sets (piernas) to create canastas (7+ tile melds). The game features muertos (extra hands) picked up by first players to empty their initial hand.

content.text: Burako is a Canasta-like Rummy game played in Argentina using 106 numbered tiles (similar to Rummikub tiles). Four players in partnerships meld sequences (escaleras) and sets (piernas) to create canastas (7+ tile melds). The game features muertos (extra hands) picked up by first players to empty their initial hand.

Burako is the Argentinean tile version of Buraco, which originated in South America in the 1940s. While Brazil developed Buraco with cards, Argentina adapted it to use tiles similar to those used in Rummikub and Turkish Okey.
4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite)
106 tiles: two of each number 1-13 in four colors (black, blue, red, yellow) plus two jokers (comodÃ­n). Tiles are placed on racks so each player sees only their own tiles.
106 Burako tiles with racks, table space for melds
Tiles mixed face down. Each player draws 11 tiles onto their rack. Two face-down stacks of 11 tiles (muertos) set aside. Remaining 40 tiles form stock in four piles of 10.

items.text: Burako 2000: Same rules but target score is 2000 instead of 3000. Shorter game suitable for quick sessions.
Two-player Burako: Two players each play two hands (left and right). Each player manages both hands but may not look at one hand when playing the other. Shared muertos; first to reach target wins.
